about: The artifact tag as read off raw text, by the server (findArtifactLineOutsideBlocks) and the SDK (artifactTag). Malloy's lexer is the authority: a ##| opener consumes its whole line, and a block closes only at a later line's start, at the opener's column. `tag` is the tag's lines, each trimmed, or null for none. `server` overrides `tag` for the server alone, with `why`.

cases.name: a one-line ## tag
a ##| block tag over several lines
cases.source:
##| artifact { kind=notebook
  tiles=[
    "s -> v"
  ]
}
|##
run: x

cases.name: a ##| block tag in CRLF
cases.source:
##| artifact { kind=notebook
  tiles=[
    "s -> v"
  ]
}
|##
run: x

cases.name: a same-line |## does not close the block: it runs to the next closer
cases.source:
##| artifact { kind=dashboard } |##
source: s is t
##|(markdown) intro
hi
|##
run: x

cases.name: a same-line |## with no later closer leaves the block unclosed
cases.why: The file does not compile (`unclosed-block-annotation`). The server's write gate still reads the opener as a tag so the write reaches the compiler, whose error says to close the block, instead of being refused as untagged.

cases.name: a |## inside a string in the block body does not close it
cases.source:
##| artifact { kind=notebook title="a |## b"
}
|##
run: x

cases.name: a |## at a line start inside a SQL string is no opener and hides nothing
cases.source:
## artifact { kind=dashboard }
source: s is duckdb.sql("""
|##
""")

cases.name: a |## after // on the opener line is still the opener's
a closer indented past the opener's column does not close it
a tag-like line inside a ##|" block body is prose
a tile's kind=text is inside the tag, not a tag of its own
cases.source:
## artifact { kind=notebook tiles=[intro { kind=text }, "s -> v"] }
##|(markdown) intro
# Hi
|##
run: x

cases.name: an untagged file
cases.source:
source: s is t
run: s -> v
